messages:
alex: Quick spike — found a handful of subtle gaps when trying to collapse the hosted / dedicated / private surfaces into a single control/runtime contract. Sketched issues below, pasted examples, and a tiny handshake proto. Looking for sanity-checks and any missing failure modes.

riley: Can you drop the sketch and call out the concrete failure cases?

alex: TL;DR: most gaps fall into 5 classes: auth/secret semantics, network topology & routing, capability/version negotiation, telemetry/PII invariants, and rollout/rollback semantics. Examples:
- Hosted issues: platform-issued API tokens + internal KMS, predictable public egress, ephemeral scaling.
- Private issues: customer KMS/HSM URIs, VPC/no-egress, custom model build (quantized artifacts), stricter compliance logs.

Concrete surprising behaviors we saw in the spike:
1) Secret normalization: hosted uses KMS references we resolve; private expects customer-provided URIs. If control-plane blindly passes secret refs to runtime, on-prem runtime can't resolve them.
2) Capability mismatch: runtime reports support for model_x_quantized but control plane assumes compatibility with model_x_bf16; fallback logic misroutes traffic.
3) Telemetry redaction: hosted telemetry has aggregated tokens and user hashes; private customers require full redaction of PII before it leaves runtime.
4) Rollout semantics: canary in hosted uses traffic-shifting; in private we often run side-by-side and we need an explicit "drain" notification to runtime.

riley: Sounds right. I think we should separate: a minimal control-plane handshake contract (capabilities + secret refs + routing tags + schema ver) and a runtime-side contract (how secrets are resolved, what telemetry is emitted, how rollouts are applied). That keeps hosting-specific translation in the control plane.

jamie: For secret_refs — we should standardize a URI format and translation rules. Example: 

```
{"secret_ref": "kms://aws/arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abc", "resolution_hint": "hosted:internal-kms, private:passthrough"}
```

The runtime can expose an optional resolver shim if it's behind a firewall (i.e., control-plane sends a short-lived token + endpoint for runtime to fetch).

alex: Good call. Two quick followups: how do we express optional features vs required capabilities, and what do we do when runtime declares capabilities but cannot meet SLOs (e.g., latency)?

taylor: Capability negotiation should include numeric constraints so control plane can make routing decisions: e.g., {"max_batch_tokens": 2048, "latency_slo_ms": 50, "quant_modes": ["int8","fp16"]}. If runtime can't meet an SLO, control plane should have a fallback policy: route to alternate model variant or degrade to best-effort with explicit header in response. Also we need a clear visibility signal so product teams can set alerts. :thinking:

morgan: On versioning: propose semantic handshake versions and a compatibility window. Runtimes must advertise supported handshake versions and a deprecation timestamp. Control plane keeps a translator component for one major version back. Also add a migration tool that can be run in private deployments to simulate hosted behavior before switching.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for control-plane/handshake-translator (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

riley: One more edge case — bring-your-own-model binaries. Private runtime may ship a model compiled with fused kernels we don't have in hosted. We need an explicit "binary_compat" capability and a fallback policy that allows control-plane to pick a compatible runtime or to reject if no compatible runtime exists. Also recording artifact metadata (quant type, opset, kernel hints) is required.

alex: Nice. Proposed next steps:
- Draft a short RFC with the handshake proto, capability schema, and secret_ref URI spec (owners: alex, riley, jamie).
- Prototype a translation shim in control-plane that maps hosted internal refs -> private passthrough and vice-versa.
- Add telemetry redaction knobs and a runtime opt-in for raw traces (customer controlled).

If anyone sees a missing catastrophic failure mode (network partition, secret leakage, silent QoS mismatch) call it out now. Otherwise I'll create the RFC doc and schedule a 30m sync. /cc @riley @jamie :shipit:

riley: I have one nit: add an explicit "drain_and_shutdown" signal for rollbacks in private (we had a messy rollback last quarter).

jamie: +1. I'll help write the secret_ref section and the example translation logic.

alex: Great — I'll open the RFC and ping for review when deploy finishes. Thanks all.
